earliestResponsibleBranch.branch: the SECOND statement of the function - the punctuation test - which runs before the values guard and before every other rule
earliestResponsibleBranch.retracedAfterCanaries2to10: Yes. The audit's original diagnosis named this line and it is still exact: nothing in canaries #2-#10 touched the punctuation test. It is the first branch to grant an accounted disposition, and it fires before anything else can.
earliestResponsibleBranch.secondBranchOnTheSamePath: Had only the punctuation test been widened, the fragment would have fallen through to the STRUCTURAL_NOISE branch: WORD_RE is [A-Za-z]-only, so contentWords scores zero words for any non-Latin text and the fragment would have been dismissed as 'the residue of splitting a parent unit'. Verified by reasoning through the flow before patching; both are on the directly responsible path and both were closed.

asciiAssumptionResponsible.primary: `!/[A-Za-z0-9]/.test(trimmed)` -> PUNCTUATION_OR_DELIMITER. 'No ASCII alphanumerics' was taken to mean 'punctuation and delimiters only'. A Chinese sentence has zero ASCII letters, so it satisfied the test perfectly.
asciiAssumptionResponsible.secondary: `WORD_RE = /[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'-]*/g` feeding contentWords, which feeds the STRUCTURAL_NOISE test. Any script outside Basic Latin produces zero content words.
asciiAssumptionResponsible.scopeOfAudit: only the directly responsible path was audited, per §4. WORD_RE itself was NOT rewritten - it still drives the closed-class filter, the nominal-label tests and connective ownership exactly as before. No repository-wide Unicode refactor.

genericInvariantImplemented.invariant: NON-LATIN TEXT IS NOT PUNCTUATION. Punctuation is the absence of any letter or digit in ANY script, and a letter the ASCII word scanner cannot see is substantive content that no rule can prove is formatting. Unknown is accountable.
genericInvariantImplemented.change1: punctuation test is now `!/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u` - Unicode property escapes, script-agnostic
genericInvariantImplemented.change2: carriesUnexplainedLetters = /\p{L}/u over the fragment with enumerators and ASCII letters removed; the STRUCTURAL_NOISE branch declines when it is set, and an explicit UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE reason is returned at the end after every positive structural rule has had first refusal (the canary #6 ordering lesson)
genericInvariantImplemented.whatItDoesNot: no Chinese/Japanese/Korean detection, no CJK character list, no CJK legal vocabulary, no translation, no linguistic tokenisation, no special case for the historical phrase. The rule detects letters, not languages.
genericInvariantImplemented.structuralFramesUnaffected: pagination, bare citations, numbered captions, quoted labels, connective ownership and punctuation dispositions all verified unchanged - none of them can claim a non-Latin fragment, and none was modified

productionFilesChanged: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-accountability/source-coverage.ts - punctuation test widened to Unicode letters/digits; carriesUnexplainedLetters guard added to the STRUCTURAL_NOISE branch with an explicit terminal reason
